nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex square matrix indexed by a nonempty finite set. Then the operator norm of $A$ with respect to the Euclidean ($\ell^2$) norm equals the largest real part of a root of the characteristic polynomial of $A$. Since these roots are real, this is its largest root.
nodes.title: Spectral norm of a positive semidefinite matrix

nodes.summary: For a Hermitian matrix $A$ indexed by a nonempty finite set, $\lambda_{\max}(A) = \max_i \lambda_i(A)$ is its largest eigenvalue. Its variational description $\lambda_{\max}(A) = \max_{\|u\| = 1} \langle u, A u\rangle$ is the top case of the Courant–Fischer theorem, and for a positive-semidefinite $A$ it equals the spectral norm.

nodes.summary: For a Hermitian matrix $A$ and a real number $\theta$, the real part of $\operatorname{tr} e^{\theta A}$ is $\sum_i e^{\theta\lambda_i(A)}$. (The trace is real; the real part is how the real-valued statements of this topic read it.)
nodes.title: Real trace exponential in terms of eigenvalues

nodes.summary: Let $J = \begin{bmatrix} I & 0 \\ 0 & -I \end{bmatrix}$ be the signature matrix of the block decomposition. Then $J\,\mathscr{H}(B)\,J = -\mathscr{H}(B)$. Since $J^2 = I$, the matrices $\mathscr{H}(B)$ and $-\mathscr{H}(B)$ are similar, so the eigenvalues of $\mathscr{H}(B)$ are symmetric about $0$.
nodes.title: The spectrum of the Hermitian dilation is symmetric
